name: Style Presets
description:
Named bundles (e.g. 'cartoon', 'realistic', 'retro') that combine a color palette, mesh style, and material settings into one switchable visual theme. The theme covers the INTERFACE as well as the world, and it did not: the preset decided contrast, scanlines and vignette, while every readout on screen carried its own hard-coded panel colours. Four byte-identical copies of the same panel-drawing helper had grown across the runtime, each brick painting the same near-black plate with the same amber hairline, and none of them switchable. A named look that restyles the world and leaves the HUD alone is half a look, and the alternative — a second component owning interface chrome — would be two components owning one idea, which is the failure this catalogue exists to avoid.

So `style` carries `hud` now, and whatever draws a panel asks for it. A build with no style_presets gets the default plate, which is what every one of those four copies was drawing anyway.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.
Upstream module named; no adapter written.

inputs.name: presetName
inputs.description: Which named look to use. Ships with `torch` (the warm near-black plate this catalogue's rooms use), `slate` (cool, low-contrast, for a build that wants the interface to recede), `retro` (scanlines and a green phosphor readout) and `cartoon`. An unknown name falls back to the first rather than failing, because a typo in a theme should not stop a game booting.

outputs.name: activePreset
outputs.description: The resolved preset: the world half (contrast, scanlines, vignette) and the interface half (`hud` — plate, border, text, accent, and the muted text a secondary line uses). Both halves in one object because they are one decision: a theme whose interface does not move with its world is a theme somebody will forget to switch.
